trait.name: Ninja
trait.text:
Ninjas are specialists in stealth, scouting, and sudden violence. They are trained to move quietly, gather information, and strike at the right moment, then disappear before enemies can respond. Some serve a clan or a patron, carrying out missions that require secrecy. Others work as free agents, selling their skills to whoever pays, or to causes they believe in. A ninja's training focuses on discipline and control. You learn how to hide, climb, and escape pursuit, as well as how to read patrol routes and pick the best target. Many also study disguises, codes, and poisons to solve problems without open combat. In war, ninjas sabotage supplies and remove key threats. In peace, they handle dangerous work that authorities cannot or will not touch.
Source: Book of Classes - Ninja (Homebrew)

feature.name: Starting Ninja
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Ninja, you begin play with 8 + your Constitution modifier hit points.
You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.
• Armor: light armor • Weapons: simple weapons, hand crossbows, shortswords, scimitars, shortbows • Tools: thieves' tools, poisoner's kit • Skills: Choose 3 from Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Stealth
You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.
• (a) a shortsword or (b) two daggers • (a) a shortbow and quiver of arrows (20) or (b) a a hand crossbow and 20 bolts • (a) a burglar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack • (a) a disguise kit or (b) a poisoner's kit • Leather armor and traveler's clothes
If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 4d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.
Source: Book of Classes p. 156 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Multiclass Ninja
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose ninja as one of your classes.
Ability Score Minimum: As a multiclass character, you must have at least the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a ninja.
• Dexterity 13
Proficiencies Gained: When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of your new class's starting proficiencies, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a rogue.
• Armor: light armor • Weapons: none • Tools: thieves' tools • Skills: Choose 1 from Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Investigation, Perception, Sleight of Hand and Stealth
Source: Book of Classes p. 156 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Multiclass Features
feature.text:
When you gain a new level in a class, you get its features for that level. You don't, however, receive the class's starting equipment, and a few features have additional rules when you're multiclassing: Channel Divinity, Extra Attack, Unarmored Defense, and Spellcasting.
Channel Divinity: If you already have the Channel Divinity feature and gain a level in a class that also grants the feature, you gain the Channel Divinity effects granted by that class, but getting the feature again doesn't give you an additional use of it. You gain additional uses only when you reach a class level that explicitly grants them to you. For example, if you are a cleric 6/paladin 4, you can use Channel Divinity twice between rests because you are high enough level in the cleric class to have more uses. Whenever you use the feature, you can choose any of the Channel Divinity effects available to you from your two classes.
Extra Attack: If you gain the Extra Attack class feature from more than one class, the features don't add together. You can't make more than two attacks with this feature unless it says you do (as the fighter's version of Extra Attack does). Similarly, the warlock's eldritch invocation Thirsting Blade doesn't give you additional attacks if you also have Extra Attack.
Unarmored Defense: If you already have the Unarmored Defense feature, you can't gain it again from another class.
Spellcasting: Your capacity for spellcasting depends partly on your combined levels in all your spellcasting classes and partly on your individual levels in those classes. Once you have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, use the rules below. If you multiclass but have the Spellcasting feature from only one class, you follow the rules as described in that class.
Spells Known and Prepared: You determine what spells you know and can prepare for each class individually, as if you were a single-classed member of that class. If you are a ranger 4/wizard 3, for example, you know three 1 st-level ranger spells based on your levels in the ranger class. As a 3rd-level wizard, you know three wizard cantrips, and your spellbook contains ten wizard spells, two of which (the two you gained when you reached 3rd level as a wizard) can be 2nd-level spells. If your Intelligence is 16, you can prepare six wizard spells from your spellbook. Each spell you know and prepare is associated with one of your classes, and you use the spell casting ability of that class when you cast the spell. Similarly, a spellcasting focus, such as a holy symbol, can be used only for the spells from the class associated with that focus. If a cantrip of yours increases in power at higher levels, the increase is based on your character level, not your level in a particular class.
Spell Slots: You determine your available spell slots by adding together all your levels in the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, and wizard classes, half your levels (rounded down) in the paladin and ranger classes, and a third of your fighter or rogue levels (rounded down) if you have the Eldritch Knight or the Arcane Trickster feature. Use this total to determine your spell slots by consulting the Multiclass Spellcaster table. If you have more than one spellcasting class, this table might give you spell slots of a level that is higher than the spells you know or can prepare. You can use those slots, but only to cast your lower-level spells. If a lower level spell that you cast, like burning hands, has an enhanced effect when cast using a higher-level slot, you can use the enhanced effect, even though you don't have any spells of that higher level. For example, if you are the aforementioned ranger 4/ wizard 3, you count as a 5th-level character when determining your spell slots: you have four 1st-level slots, three 2nd-level slots, and two 3rd-level slots. However, you don't know any 3rd-level spells, nor do you know any 2nd-level ranger spells. You can use the spell slots of those levels to cast the spells you do know-and potentially enhance their effects.
Pact Magic: If you have both the Spellcasting class feature and the Pact Magic class feature from the warlock class, you can use the spell slots you gain from the Pact Magic feature to cast spells you know or have prepared from classes with the Spellcasting class feature, and you can use the spell slots you gain from the Spellcasting class feature to cast warlock spells you know.
Source: Player's Handbook (2014) p. 164

feature.name: Killing Intent
feature.text:
Your focus narrows until one life in the battle seems to carry all the weight of the moment. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet; the mark lasts for 1 minute, until you are incapacitated, or until you mark another creature. The first time on each of your turns that you hit the marked creature with a weapon attack, you deal extra damage equal to your Killing Intent dice (see the Ninja table). This extra damage is the same type as the weapon's damage. In addition, after you deal this extra damage, you can either move up to 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks from the marked creature, provided your speed is not 0, or force the marked creature to have disadvantage on the next opportunity attack it makes before the start of your next turn.
Ninja: Level | Killing Intent 1 | 1d4 2 | 1d4 3 | 2d4 4 | 2d4 5 | 3d4 6 | 3d4 7 | 4d4 8 | 4d4 9 | 5d4 10 | 5d4 11 | 6d4 12 | 6d4 13 | 7d4 14 | 7d4 15 | 8d4 16 | 8d4 17 | 9d4 18 | 9d4 19 | 10d4 20 | 10d4
Source: Book of Classes p. 158 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Roofline Traverse
feature.text:
A straight path is for people who expect to be seen. As a bonus action, you enter a flowing ascent until the end of the current turn. During that time, you gain a climb speed equal to your speed, you can move across vertical surfaces and liquids without falling during the movement, and opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage. You can take this bonus action at any point during your movement. If you end that movement in dim light, darkness, or behind cover, you can attempt to Hide as part of the same bonus action, provided you otherwise meet the normal requirements for hiding. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 158 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Credos
feature.text:
At 3rd level, you commit to a Credo that shapes your craft: Credo of the Moon, Credo of the Lotus, or Credo of the Blade. Your Credo grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 158 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1, or you can choose a feat. You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
If your DM allows it, you can choose your class's optional feature at 4th level instead of increasing an ability score or choosing a feat. If you do, you gain that optional feature's 4th-level benefit. You cannot choose this optional feature for the first time at 8th level or higher. At 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you choose either the corresponding benefit of that optional feature or an Ability Score Improvement or feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 157 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Blade Tempest (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
Your momentum becomes its own weapon. As a bonus action, you surge for 1 minute. Your speed increases by 20 feet, you ignore difficult terrain, and once on each of your turns you can make one additional weapon attack when you take the Attack action. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 162 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Whispering Return (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
A lone steel star hums from your palm and always finds its way back. You have one Crescent Shuriken, and you are proficient with it. The Crescent Shuriken is a simple weapon. It deals 1d4 piercing damage and has the finesse and thrown (range 20/60) properties. It is a magic weapon, and you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. It returns to your hand immediately after you make a ranged attack with it. When you take the Attack action and throw the shuriken, you can use a bonus action to throw it again. If the shuriken is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it over the course of a short or long rest. If you recreate the shuriken while the previous one still exists, the previous shuriken loses its magic.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Substitution Art
feature.text:
The strike finds cloth, splinters, and empty space where your body should have been. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Ninja level. You can then teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet that is in dim light, darkness, or behind cover. Until the start of your next turn, the space you left becomes lightly obscured by a fleeting afterimage, puff of dust, or burst of cloth scraps (your choice each time). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 158 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Fold Through the Gap
feature.text:
You read the shape of danger a heartbeat before it closes. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, and your speed is not 0, you can move up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see without provoking opportunity attacks, provided you are not incapacitated and are wearing no medium or heavy armor and using no shield. You make the saving throw after this movement. If this movement takes you completely out of the effect's area, you automatically succeed on the saving throw.
Source: Book of Classes p. 158 (Homebrew)

You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. If your DM allows it, you can choose your class's optional feature at 4th level instead of increasing an ability score or choosing a feat. If you do, you gain that optional feature's 4th-level benefit. You cannot choose this optional feature for the first time at 8th level or higher. At 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you choose either the corresponding benefit of that optional feature or an Ability Score Improvement or feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 157 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Gale Arc (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
Your star skims lantern smoke and trims corners of shadow. The shuriken's thrown range becomes 30/90. Your attacks with it ignore half cover, and three-quarters cover counts as half cover for you. In addition, when you miss with an attack roll using the shuriken, you can reroll the attack roll. Once you use this reroll, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 162 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Silent Alchemy
feature.text:
Your kit whispers: powder, resin, bite, and every dose carries more than simple sickness. During a short or long rest, you can create a number of toxin doses equal to your proficiency bonus using a poisoner's kit; unused doses lose their potency when you finish your next short or long rest. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend a dose to force it to make a Constitution saving throw against your save DC. The creature makes this saving throw even if it is immune to the poisoned condition. On a failure, it is poisoned until the end of your next turn. If the creature is immune to the poisoned condition, it instead has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of your next turn. You can expend only one dose created by this class on a single attack.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Prepared Route
feature.text:
Before violence starts, your escape is already chosen. When you roll initiative and are not surprised, choose up to three unoccupied spaces you can see within 30 feet of you that are in dim light, darkness, or behind cover. Until the end of your second turn, once on each of your turns, if you are in one of those chosen spaces, you can teleport to another chosen space as part of your movement. In addition, the first time you hit a creature during the first round of combat, you can mark it with Killing Intent without using a bonus action, and that hit can deal your Killing Intent damage as if the creature had been marked before the attack hit.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement

If your DM allows it, you can choose your class's optional feature at 4th level instead of increasing an ability score or choosing a feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 157 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Razor Sigil (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
A thin tone rides the throw and unravels footing. The shuriken now grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with it, the target takes an extra 1d4 psychic damage, and its speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Quiet Mastery
feature.text:
You do not merely hide; you pass through a place without letting it keep a memory of you. You cannot be tracked by nonmagical means unless you choose to leave a trail. In addition, creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to find you while you are hidden. When you miss with a ranged weapon attack made while hidden, that attack does not reveal your position unless the ammunition's path, impact, or the surrounding circumstances would clearly do so.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Nerve Strike
feature.text:
Your blade kisses a tendon. Once per turn when you deal extra damage from Killing Intent, you can impose one effect on that target until the start of your next turn: its speed is reduced by 10 feet, it cannot take reactions, or it has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

Source: Book of Classes p. 157 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Shadow Pin (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
The star nails a fleeing shadow to stone. When you hit a creature with the shuriken while it is on the ground or within 5 feet of a solid surface, such as a wall, ceiling, pillar, or tree, you can force it to make a Dexterity saving throw against your save DC. On a failed save, the creature is restrained until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Shadow Relay
feature.text:
Darkness becomes a lattice you traverse. While you are in dim light or darkness, you can move through hostile creatures' spaces, but you cannot willingly end your movement in another creature's space, and opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage. In addition, once on each of your turns, you can teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space in dim light or darkness that you can see.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1, or you can choose a feat. If you choose an Ability Score Improvement or feat at one of those levels, you forfeit the optional feature's benefit at that level.
Source: Book of Classes p. 157 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Night's Comet (Optional Feature)
feature.text:
A falling crescent stitches space between you and your mark. The shuriken now grants a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. Attacks you make with it do not suffer disadvantage at long range, and they ignore all cover short of total cover. In addition, once on each of your turns after you hit a creature with the shuriken, you can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of that creature.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Crescent Hour
feature.text:
The night crowns you, and time holds its breath. As a bonus action, you enter a focused state for 1 minute. When you activate this feature, you can immediately mark one creature you can see within 60 feet with Killing Intent without using another action. While this state lasts, the extra damage from Killing Intent can apply to two separate hits on each of your turns, and you can take the Hide action as a bonus action. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 159 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Credo: Credo of the Blade
feature.text:
Rooftops blur beneath your feet as steel sings in a wheeling arc, swift as a stormfront. You ride momentum like a creed, striking, sliding, and standing elsewhere before the echo fades.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Blade Flurry (Credo of the Blade)
feature.text:
Your weapons blur into a wheeling storm. When you take the Attack action with a finesse or thrown weapon, you can make one additional attack with a dagger or dart as a bonus action. You can draw or stow the dagger or dart as part of the attack. You can add your ability modifier to the damage of this bonus attack.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Windrunner (Credo of the Blade)
feature.text:
Your footwork rides the pressure wave of each cut. Your speed increases by 10 feet. When you make a long jump or high jump, you can use Dexterity instead of Strength to determine the distance or height of the jump. In addition, you take no damage from the first 20 feet of a fall, and you land on your feet if you are not incapacitated.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Turn the Tide (Credo of the Blade)
feature.text:
One strike flows into repositioning. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can immediately move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks, or you can move the target 5 feet to an unoccupied space on a surface it can occupy that you can see, provided the target is no more than one size larger than you.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Aerial Reversal (Credo of the Blade)
feature.text:
You pivot around a whistling blade. When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to move up to 10 feet and make one weapon attack against that creature. You must make the attack with a weapon that can reach the target. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Blade Tempest (Credo of the Blade)
feature.text:
Your momentum becomes its own weapon. As a bonus action, you surge for 1 minute. Your speed increases by 20 feet, you ignore difficult terrain, and once on each of your turns you can make one additional weapon attack when you take the Attack action. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Credo: Credo of the Lotus
feature.text:
A teacup steams; a single petal falls; a pulse slows beneath your calm gaze. You master tincture and tendon, laying quiet ruin with toxins and precise, mercifully brief pressure.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Lotus Brewer (Credo of the Lotus)
feature.text:
You steep death like tea, and even the hardiest blood hesitates when your craft takes hold. During a short or long rest, you can prepare a number of Lotus doses equal to your proficiency bonus using a poisoner's kit; unused doses lose their potency when you finish your next short or long rest. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend a dose to deal 2d6 poison damage and force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw against your save DC. You can expend only one dose created by this class on a single attack. The poison damage is still affected by resistance or immunity. The creature makes this saving throw even if it has immunity to poison damage or the poisoned condition. On a failed save, the creature is poisoned until the end of your next turn. If it is immune to the poisoned condition, it instead cannot take the Dash or Disengage action until the start of your next turn.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Serpent's Resilience (Credo of the Lotus)
feature.text:
Toxin tastes like iron and resolve. You have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against poison. In addition, you cannot poison yourself when applying or brewing toxins using a poisoner's kit.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Seeping Venom (Credo of the Lotus)
feature.text:
A bruise blooms into a creeping hush, and even bodies that reject the venom still falter under your precise delivery. When a creature fails a saving throw against your Lotus Brewer or Silent Alchemy, it also cannot take reactions until the start of your next turn. This effect can apply even if the creature is immune to the poisoned condition.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Body Lock (Credo of the Lotus)
feature.text:
A knuckle taps a secret in the spine. When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw against your save DC. On a failure, it is restrained until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Lotus Cataclysm (Credo of the Lotus)
feature.text:
A single cut carries midnight. When a creature fails a saving throw against your Lotus Brewer or Body Lock, you can replace the condition or secondary non-poison effect it would suffer with the stunned condition until the end of your next turn. Any damage still occurs. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Credo: Credo of the Moon
feature.text:
Lantern light kisses a painted mask as you flow through courts and alleyways with borrowed names and measured smiles. You turn doubt into cover, walking past guards as if expected and leaving only rumors where footprints should be.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Maskcraft (Credo of the Moon)
feature.text:
With a brushstroke and posture, you are someone else. You gain proficiency with the forgery kit and one language of your choice. You can create a convincing disguise over the course of 1 minute. You have advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks made to maintain a false identity you prepared with a disguise kit.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Moon Vanish (Credo of the Moon)
feature.text:
Your outline flickers like candlelight. As a bonus action, you become invisible until the end of your next turn or until you attack or force a saving throw. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Soft Words, Sharp Truths (Credo of the Moon)
feature.text:
Your voice is a key that fits most locks. Choose Deception or Persuasion. You gain proficiency in the chosen skill if you do not already have it, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses that skill. In addition, when you spend 1 minute speaking privately with a creature, you learn one mundane personal detail about it of the DM's choice.
Source: Book of Classes p. 160 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Unseen Exit (Credo of the Moon)
feature.text:
You leave only a rumor behind. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to become invisible and move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks. The invisibility ends at the end of the movement or if you attack. You can use this feature once per short or long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Perfect Double (Credo of the Moon)
feature.text:
Your shadow steps away and smiles. As an action, you create a quasi-real double in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. The double lasts for 1 minute, does not move, has your AC and 1 hit point, can be targeted by attacks as if it were a creature, and vanishes if it is reduced to 0 hit points. As a bonus action, you can swap places with the double if you can see it within 30 feet of you. When a creature targets you with an attack and the double is also a valid target for that attack, you can use your reaction before the attack roll is made to have the attack target the double instead. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
Source: Book of Classes p. 161 (Homebrew)
